claim: Species whose first post-listing assessment is a legacy category

claim: Category transitions between comparable global and European assessments
operative_definition: One step between consecutive comparable assessments, global or European, of the same species inside 1982-2025, ordered by year and assessment id; both rows of a same-year pair stay in the sequence, as the published method always counted them. A non-comparable assessment breaks the series rather than being stepped over. A transition requires a DIFFERENT category: redlist_scale.transitions appends only when the rank changes, so a pair that holds its category is not a transition and the total is not the number of consecutive comparable pairs. That condition was missing from this definition until 6 October 2026, when the definition lens of round u15 found the same looseness in the two copies in the manuscript; this file exists to stop exactly that, and it was loose in the same way. The scale is the one in ingest/redlist_scale.py, under which LR/cd reads as Near Threatened per the crosswalk the Methods cite and Regionally Extinct is not on the ladder. Recorded as 34 until 6 October 2026, when this number was found to have been computed on a second, divergent rank table that excluded LR/cd while the species split in the same sentence used one that did not; the two transitions it could not see are the polar bear's 1996 LR/cd to 2006 VU and Dall's porpoise's 1996 LR/cd to 2008 LC. From 21 October 2026 European regional assessments are included (the lead author's decision): for each species the Global and Europe assessments form one series ordered by year and assessment id, the higher assessment id standing in a year with several, and the Mediterranean porbeagle assessment (16527805) is excluded.

claim: Species whose current category, on the latest global or European assessment, is CR (Critically Endangered)
operative_definition: Most recent assessment per species, global or European, within 1982-2025, counted by category. Each species contributes exactly once, so the seven counts (C23 to C28 and C148, Regionally Extinct) sum to the 43 species in the study set. Categories are not mapped: the most recent assessment of every species uses a 2001-system category, so no legacy crosswalk applies here. Where a species carries several assessments in its final year the higher assessment id stands (redlist_scale.pick_in_year) and the is_latest flag must agree with it; two species are decided this way (Bubo scandiacus 2021, LC against VU; Odobenus rosmarus 2025, NT against VU). Until 6 October 2026 the tie was broken by CSV row order, which reported the superseded assessment as current for those two species and gave VU 7, NT 4, LC 22. claim: Records reported from both ends on the exact eight-field match
operative_definition: Records whose eight-field key -- species, year, importer, exporter, term, unit, purpose and source -- occurs under both reporter sides, counted as records rather than as keys. C66 is the exact join Methods describes. C67 is the same join with the year dropped, and it is larger, which is why the paper reports C66 as a LOWER BOUND on the both-ends overlap: the two reporter sides disagree on exactly these fields -- a consignment leaving in December and clearing in January is two different years -- so an exact match misses the hard cases and leaves them looking independent. Relaxing term, unit or purpose instead also enlarges the set (281,875 / 269,158 / 270,342); the year is named in the paper because it is the largest.

claim: Genuine category transitions on global and European assessments, 1982-2025
operative_definition: Sensitivity of the trajectory balance to the 2001 revision of the IUCN criteria, which is the strongest objection put to the paper's near-even split of 22 improvements and 21 deteriorations. Instrument 1 holds the criteria fixed WITHIN each comparison by bucketing every genuine transition on the global-and-European series in 1982-2025 on where the 2001 revision falls relative to its two endpoints: C133 to C135 are transitions whose endpoints are both 2001 or later, which cannot cross the revision, with their two directions; C136 straddles it and C137 falls wholly before it. C132 is the total and must equal the three buckets. Transitions come from redlist_scale.transitions on the global-and-European series, so a non-comparable assessment breaks the chain rather than being skipped over and same-year ties go through the one tie-break. Instrument 2 (C138 to C140) restricts each species' global-and-European series to assessments published in 2001 or later and reclassifies it; it is harsher and it does NOT isolate the revision, because restricting the start year also shortens the window from 43 years to 24, which reduces movement independently of any criteria change. Neither instrument bounds category change arising from improved knowledge or from taxonomy within one criteria era: that needs IUCN's reason-for-change field, which the deposited series does not carry. The verifier refuses if fewer than half the transitions are post-revision, since the instrument would then bound nothing. From 21 October 2026 European regional assessments are included (the lead author's decision): for each species the Global and Europe assessments form one series ordered by year and assessment id, the higher assessment id standing in a year with several, and the Mediterranean porbeagle assessment (16527805) is excluded.

Instrument 2 (C138 to C140) restricts each species' global-and-European series to assessments published in 2001 or later and reclassifies it; it is harsher and it does NOT isolate the revision, because restricting the start year also shortens the window from 43 years to 24, which reduces movement independently of any criteria change. Neither instrument bounds category change arising from improved knowledge or from taxonomy within one criteria era: that needs IUCN's reason-for-change field, which the deposited series does not carry. The verifier refuses if fewer than half the transitions are post-revision, since the instrument would then bound nothing.
